newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-NYMEX futures range up, but weaker later.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-NYMEX futures range up, but weaker later.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20

* Some analysts fancied a buying extreme to take the gasoline market back towards 59 cents, but most felt this would be followed by a further downside move given the bearish underlying fundamentals. * In the short term crude remains stuck in a fairly wide range with little convincing evidence for a break out.
NYMEX crude and products may get a lift from buying as shorts lock in profits, but while markets are expected to hold range, longer term sentiment remains bearish, analysts said.

Gasoline remains in neutral preparation. The 14-day RSI is creeping back into the oversold region but this is countered by the divergence of the 10 and 20-day moving averages offering little sign of a move away from the current low levels, but support is in place around 56 cents.

On Thursday July gasoline slipped below key technical support of 56.00 cents a gallon to 55.90 cents it's lowest level for just under 15 months on fundamental oversupply and poor demand pressures, but analysts said it was too unconvincing a break to be considered definitive.
The contract tested and held the 56.00 cent level three consecutive sessions last week.
"Safely back in the range we are left with little else to but bounce from one end to the other waiting for a break," said Fenella Graham at MeesPierson.

"As before we remain wary of any potential break, ready to join the downside where preparation allows or holding back to see if a buying extreme appears to allow us to join the upside breaks". Graham said.
Some analysts fancied the buying extreme to take the market back towards 59 cents, but most felt this would be followed by a further downside move given the bearish underlying fundamentals.
With little fundamental support coming from products analysts said WTI will have to continue to rely on technical indicators for support.

In the short term the crude market remains stuck in a fairly wide range with little convincing evidence for a break out but even if short covering lifts the market ahead of OPEC analysts were expecting longer term weakness to eventually prevail.
"The manner in which prices fell yesterday did not close the door on re-visiting $19.47 before $18.41 support cracks," said Al Graham at Elliott Wave International, Gainesville, Georgia.
Howard Friend at MCM said the key to any fresh upside strength lies in the double bottom targets at $19.24 and $19.62 on the August chart.
"All the time we stay below these levels the bearish sentiment will persist," Friend said.
